slides.heading: Nested Conditionals
slides.body: Nested Conditionals is part of Conditional Execution. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Nested Conditionals
slides.body: A nested conditional places one if statement inside another. It is useful when one decision depends on another decision first.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Nested conditionals are like entering a building, then checking the room number after you are already inside.

slides.body: A conditional needs a colon, correct indentation, and a condition that clearly evaluates to True or False.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use nested if statements to print Verified only if email_ok and password_ok are both True.
slides.hint: Write the password check inside the email check.

quiz.prompt_text: What is a nested conditional in Python?

options: An if statement that uses the or operator
An if statement placed inside another if statement
Two separate if statements that run one after the other
An if statement with more than three elif branches

quiz.explanation: Correct! A nested conditional is an if statement inside another if. It adds a second layer of checking after the outer condition is already True.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to enter a venue only if age is at least 18 AND the person has an ID.
quiz.explanation: age is assigned first, then has_id, then the outer if checks age, and inside it a second if checks has_id before printing Enter.

quiz.prompt_text: Use nested if statements to print Verified only if both email_ok and password_ok are True.

content.hint: Write the password check inside the email check using two levels of indentation.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: if email_ok: then indented if password_ok: then double-indented print makes both conditions required before Verified is shown.
